clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within roughly three years: your late nights and withdrawal from activities, your wrist injury stopping your playing and your break with Rafe, your low functioning and lost footing after he died, your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery, your mother's marriage to Desmond, and your sister Tara's birth. By early 1994, when you found your drive again in Portugal and your father heard nothing of your film, the worst had passed; the cluster reaches to your exchange and the rest of your degree.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002, within roughly two years: your running out of steam for performing, your disastrous audition, your distance from your parents and friends, your move away from Thornbury and into a brief relationship that ended within the year, your sinking into deep depression once you split, and your distance from your family when you returned. By early 2004, when you returned to your therapist and began to recover, and your grandmother died in February, the depth of the trouble had passed; your requests for help from your parents and your therapist sit in these months as the family settled.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2009
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within roughly a year: your time building with Silas at Alder Creek, where you could barely manage contact with your mother, her pushing to visit despite your asking her not to, your conflict with her when she came, and your cutoff once you moved to nursing school that August. Your aunt Imogen's stroke in early 2009 sits beside the period's close; by then your silence with your mother held but the acute strain had settled.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and her family's life, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within roughly two and a half years: your distance from your mother easing slightly, your cousin Alice's diagnosis with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your aunt Imogen's worsening memory loss and conflict with your cousin Hal, your sister Tara's wedding and pregnancy, your steady work and raised anxiety about driving projects forward, your sleeping pill, and your effort toward shorter regular calls with your mother. In late October 2019, at your mother-in-law Frances's retirement at the lake, you had no sleep and could only distance yourself from the gathering, while Wren grew anxious watching you; by the weeks after, the acute strain of that weekend had passed, though your anxiety and her fusion with her father and brother held on.
